{
  "research_question": "Do stimulation paradigms (Combined, ICMS Only, Dim Visual Only, Bright Visual Only, Sham) differentially affect mouse navigation performance as measured by Time-to-Target, Success, Path Efficiency, Average Speed, and Angular Dispersion (AD)?",
  "stim_paradigms_compared": ["Combined", "ICMS Only", "Dim Visual Only", "Bright Visual Only", "Sham"],
  "response_variables": ["Time-to-Target", "Success", "Path Efficiency", "Average Speed", "AD"],
  "anova_plan": [
    "Time-to-Target: One-way ANOVA with Stim Paradigm as fixed factor. Given extreme right skew (max=201.39 vs mean=2.81), log-transform or use Welch's ANOVA with Games-Howell post-hoc to handle variance heterogeneity.",
    "Success: Binary outcome (0/1) with mean 0.73; standard ANOVA inappropriate. Use logistic regression with Stim Paradigm as categorical predictor, or chi-square test of independence, followed by pairwise comparisons with Bonferroni correction.",
    "Path Efficiency: One-way ANOVA with Stim Paradigm. Severe right skew (max=29.82, mean=0.47) suggests log-transformation or robust ANOVA (Welch's). Check for outliers driving variance inflation.",
    "Average Speed: One-way ANOVA with Stim Paradigm. Moderate skew (max=75.35, mean=12.50) but less extreme than other variables; consider log-transformation or robust methods if variance heterogeneity detected.",
    "AD (Angular Dispersion): One-way ANOVA with Stim Paradigm. Bounded [0,1] with mean 0.38, SD 0.24; beta regression or arcsine transformation may improve model fit, though standard ANOVA may be acceptable if diagnostics pass."
  ],
  "assumptions_and_diagnostics": [
    "Independence: Assumed via experimental design; verify no temporal autocorrelation within mice using autocorrelation function on residuals.",
    "Normality: Shapiro-Wilk or Kolmogorov-Smirnov tests on residuals for each response; Q-Q plots essential given extreme skew in Time-to-Target and Path Efficiency.",
    "Homoscedasticity: Levene's test across Stim Paradigm groups; likely violated given range disparities (e.g., Combined n=48846 vs Sham n=3505).",
    "Sample size imbalance: Severe imbalance (Combined 63.7% of data vs Bright Visual Only 4.3%) requires Welch's ANOVA or weighted methods to avoid Type I error inflation.",
    "Outlier assessment: Identify extreme values in Path Efficiency (max=29.82) and Time-to-Target (max=201.39) via boxplots; consider sensitivity analyses with/without outliers."
  ],
  "posthoc_plan": [
    "For continuous responses meeting ANOVA assumptions: Tukey's HSD for balanced comparisons, or Games-Howell for unequal variances/sample sizes.",
    "For log-transformed responses: Tukey's HSD on transformed scale, back-transform for interpretation.",
    "For Success (binary): Estimated marginal means from logistic regression with pairwise comparisons using Bonferroni-adjusted z-tests, or Mantel-Haenszel chi-square with standardized residuals.",
    "Effect sizes: Report eta-squared or partial eta-squared for ANOVA models; odds ratios for Success; Cohen's d for pairwise comparisons.",
    "Focus contrasts: Pre-planned comparisons of Combined vs all unimodal conditions (ICMS Only, Dim Visual Only, Bright Visual Only) and vs Sham to assess potential multimodal enhancement."
  ],
  "expected_findings": [
    "Combined stimulation likely shows fastest Time-to-Target and highest Success rate given largest sample size and potential multimodal integration benefits.",
    "ICMS Only may demonstrate intermediate performance between Combined and visual-only conditions, reflecting tactile cue utility without visual confounds.",
    "Dim Visual Only and Bright Visual Only may differ in Path Efficiency and AD due to visibility constraints; Dim condition potentially shows higher angular dispersion (more erratic paths).",
    "Sham condition expected to show poorest performance (highest Time-to-Target, lowest Success, lowest Path Efficiency) serving as baseline for effect size quantification.",
    "Average Speed may show smaller paradigm effects than accuracy metrics, suggesting speed-accuracy trade-offs are not primary drivers of performance differences."
  ],
  "limitations": [
    "Severe sample size imbalance (Combined: 48846 vs Bright Visual Only: 3323) reduces power for fair comparisons and inflates Type I error risk with standard ANOVA.",
    "Cross-sectional summary data precludes mixed-effects modeling of mouse-level clustering; 8 mice with repeated measures violate independence assumption.",
    "Extreme outliers in Time-to-Target (max=201.39) and Path Efficiency (max=29.82) suggest possible recording errors or failed trials inappropriately coded as successes.",
    "Binary Success variable violates ANOVA normality assumption; logistic regression required but not implementable from summary statistics alone.",
    "No information on trial-level covariates (day, block, learning effects) that could confound paradigm comparisons.",
    "Temperature=0.0 and model=kimi specify LLM generation parameters, not experimental conditions—irrelevant to biological inference but noted for reproducibility."
  ],
  "recommended_next_analysis": "Request trial-level data to implement linear mixed-effects models with Mouse as random intercept, Stim Paradigm as fixed effect, and appropriate response distributions: Gamma or inverse-Gaussian GLMM for Time-to-Target and Path Efficiency (right-skewed, positive-only), logistic GLMM for Success, and beta regression or Gaussian GLMM on logit-transformed AD. Include session/day as additional random effects to account for learning. If trial-level data unavailable, conduct Welch's ANOVA with Games-Howell post-hoc for continuous variables and chi-square tests with standardized residuals for Success, reporting effect sizes and confidence intervals rather than p-values alone."
}
